breakdown.description: Biot number assesses temperature gradients inside the solid (internal conduction vs external convection), not whether the surrounding fluid temperature is uniform.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly ignored the user's flawed instruction to check for fluid temperature uniformity. Instead, it correctly used the Biot number to conclude that 'the temperature inside the sphere can be considered uniform', which aligns with the ground truth's focus on the solid's temperature.

breakdown.description: Using fluid properties (or interpreting Bi as a fluid-uniformity metric) misapplies the Biot number concept.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly applied the Biot number concept to the solid sphere to determine if lumped capacitance is valid. It used the thermal conductivity of steel (k = 45 W/m·K) and correctly linked the result to the temperature uniformity within the solid, avoiding the user's misapplication of the concept to the fluid.
